XLand-MiniGrid 0.9.3 (Apache-2.0): environments, goal checks and rules; byte-identical to the PyPI wheel xminigrid==0.9.3

notes: Evaluator: LIMEN's own CascadeEvaluator (limen/evaluator.py at Lossfunk/LIMEN@cf0b44da, MIT) runs unchanged in a child process with LIMEN's configs/easy_pickup.yaml: crash filter (syntax, required functions, import, dry run and jit on a real state, observation length <= 512), a cascade run of 500,000 steps with seed 42 that must reach 5 % success (otherwise that run's success rate is the score, as LIMEN's archive records it), then PPO with seeds 42, 43 and 44 for 1,000,000 steps each (7 updates of 8,192 environments x 16 steps = 917,504 steps; LIMEN divides without rounding up) and the mean success rate over 50 evaluation episodes per seed with a 80-step horizon. LIMEN's LLM-driven search (prompts, MAP-Elites archive) is not part of the task; one interface is scored per evaluation. The 46 LIMEN files are fetched by scripts/prepare_jax_station.py --limen and checked one by one against catalog/jax_station-data-lock.json. This is LIMEN's in-search fitness (Section 5.3; the 'Cascade' and 'Full' budgets of the paper's Table 3); the paper's main results instead retrain the best interface of each method from scratch with 10 seeds at 2M steps (Section 5.5; Table 3, '10-seed Eval') and report 99 % for joint search on this task, so those values are not comparable with this score.

Additions around the unchanged LIMEN code: the candidate source must pass a static policy before LIMEN sees it (imports limited to jax, jax.numpy, jax.lax, jax.nn and math, where LIMEN's own instructions allow jax and jax.numpy only; no attribute assignment; no private, file I/O, callback, configuration or experimental attributes; no exec-like builtins), and the child process has an audit hook (no subprocesses, sockets or ctypes; writes only in its private temporary directory, where LIMEN writes the candidate file). LIMEN's adapter.run_training is wrapped only to record per-run metrics, and the configuration's relative ruleset path is made absolute. The suite template imports the candidate module in the evaluator process before scoring, so module-level code runs there without these restrictions.

Hardware and software: CPU instead of the paper's single NVIDIA L4 GPU; jax/jaxlib 0.11.2, flax 0.12.10, optax 0.2.8, distrax 0.1.9 (tfp-nightly 0.26.0.dev20261010), xminigrid 0.9.3 (= dunnolab/xland-minigrid@0d306d14), numpy 2.5.3, Python 3.12; four XLA threads (NPROC/PJRT_NPROC=4) and PYTHONHASHSEED=0 in the child. LIMEN's code runs on these versions without changes.

Seed: LIMEN's default observation (the adapter's flattened grid, position, direction, pocket and step counter) with a sparse reward of 1 on the step that completes the goal, i.e. the paper's Sparse baseline ('raw simulator observations with binary success reward'; the paper's Section 5.1 describes the default observation as a flattened 7 x 7 egocentric grid, XLand-MiniGrid's own view, whereas LIMEN's code uses this full-grid observation in its default and reward-only modes, and its default mode keeps XLand-MiniGrid's built-in reward, 1 - 0.9 x step / max_steps on completion); under random actions in 4,096 environments the reward fired exactly on XLand-MiniGrid's goal events (no misses, no false positives).

Measured (validation/jax_station-checks.json; Apple M4 Max shared with other jobs, load averages 8-37): the seed scores 0.213 (seeds 42/43/44: 0.16, 0.28, 0.20; cascade run 0.14) in 104-220 s wall (322 CPU-seconds, peak memory 2.2 GB), identically in three runs; a constant-zero reward with the same observation scores 0.127 (0.10, 0.14, 0.14); LIMEN's published evolved interface (examples/evolved_interfaces/easy_pickup.py, labelled 'Success rate: 99%') scores 0.993 (1.00, 0.98, 1.00) in 190 s, reproducing the published value. Declared timeout 600 s (child limit 540 s).

Near saturation: strong interfaces reach 0.98-1.00 here, as in the paper (99 % for joint search and 100 % for observation-only search in its 10-seed retraining at 2M steps, Section 5.5; 97-100 % in-search across five search seeds, Appendix B.4), so the task separates weak from strong interfaces but hardly ranks strong ones (resolution 1/150).

Determinism: repeated evaluations of the same candidate in the evaluator's child gave identical per-run success rates, returns and episode lengths (the seed, three times). Results depend on the numerical libraries and their thread settings: with VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS (the thread count of Apple's Accelerate library) unset instead of 4, the same training of LIMEN's published easy interface gave a different final return on its 500,000-step run (6.149 instead of 6.143) and per-seed success rates differing by 0.02 (0.98 instead of 1.00 for seed 42). The evaluator fixes these variables, so scores are reproducible on the same platform and software stack but not across CPU types, BLAS/LAPACK builds or GPUs. valid is null: success rates are sampled estimates after stochastic training; near a success rate of 0.2 the standard error of the 150-episode mean is about 0.035.

sources.locator: ZAPBench activity traces 240930 (zarr v3, float32 [7879, 71721], CC-BY-4.0), downloaded over HTTPS by scripts/prepare_jax_station.py --zapbench
zapbench/constants.py and data_utils.py (condition bounds, train/val/test/test_holdout splits; Apache-2.0)
published per-condition, per-step test MAE of the ZAPBench paper's methods (used for the reference check)

notes: Reduced-budget CPU proxy (protocol recreated). Kept from the Station's ZAPBench task (dualverse-ai/station@782088e5, example/research_misc/zapbench, Apache-2.0): the candidate hooks (create_network returning init/apply with optional mutable and needs_rng, compute_loss, create_optimizer, _define_hyperparameters, BATCH_SIZE; an omitted hook falls back to a port of its defaults.py), the training loop of train_single.py (shuffled epochs, its train step, validation MAE after every epoch, early stopping with patience 20, best-validation parameters), ZAPBench's condition-aware splits for a 4-step context (process_data.py) and the test MAE. Changed: one seed (42) instead of three (BASE_SEED + 0, 1, 2; the candidate's BASE_SEED is ignored so that a seed cannot be chosen); at most 3 epochs and 600 s of training wall time on CPU with four threads (training stops before an epoch predicted to exceed the cap) instead of up to 120 epochs or 60 minutes on a 24 GB GPU; the complete() and test() hooks are ignored; Ray Tune search spaces are not accepted; BATCH_SIZE must lie in 1..64 and defaults to 8 (the value of the Station's task text and paper; its main.py falls back to 32). The default network follows defaults.py (hidden width 64), not the '4->128->32' of its baseline description.

Data: ZAPBench traces 240930 (gs://zapbench-release/volumes/20240930/traces, CC-BY-4.0) over HTTPS: 2,256 uncompressed 512 x 512 chunks checked against Google Cloud Storage MD5s; chunk manifest, full-array SHA-256 and prepared files in catalog/jax_station-data-lock.json. The split rules restate zapbench.data_utils at google-research/zapbench@7347b3b2 (the prepare script executes the pinned functions and compares): training 5,052 steps (4,772 windows), validation 749 steps (469 windows, the count the Station paper quotes), test 1,872 steps (1,557 windows: the last 20 % of the 8 training conditions plus the held-out taxis condition from 252 steps after its start). Training and validation arrays are stored as float16 (mean absolute rounding error 2.1e-05 against a mean absolute value of 0.118; at most 4.9e-04; the validation MAE of the mean-of-context predictor changes by +7.0e-09); the test array is float32, so the score uses the original values.

Isolation: training runs in a child process that can read only the training and validation arrays (audit hook; the test split is never sent to it). Its best parameters and the single-window predictor, exported with jax.export (parameters as inputs), are scored by a second child that never executes candidate Python code: the StableHLO module is checked for host callbacks, foreign custom calls and host communication (only LAPACK and sharding custom calls pass; jax.export itself refuses host callbacks), and predictions are made one window at a time (vmap over single-window apply calls with training=False) so a model cannot pool information across overlapping test windows. Validation MAE during training uses the same single-window predictor instead of the Station's batches of consecutive windows. The suite template imports the candidate module in the evaluator process before scoring, so module-level code runs there without these restrictions.

Metric: the mean over the 9 test conditions of the MAE over all stride-1 windows, the 32 predicted steps and the 71,721 neurons, i.e. ZAPBench's per-condition, per-step MAE averaged over conditions and over steps 1-32 (the 'Average' of the Station paper's Fig. 8; the Station's eval.py prints per-condition values only at steps 1, 4, 8, 16 and 32). Reference check: a parameter-free candidate that repeats the mean of the 4 context steps scores 0.031859533 through the full evaluator, ZAPBench's published 'mean' baseline (combined.json, 146317468/3) being 0.031859533; all 288 published per-condition, per-step values are reproduced within 2.0e-08 (scripts/prepare_jax_station.py --reference). Unlike this score, the Station's search score (its Research Counter's primary score) is the validation MAE averaged over its 3 seeds, and the test sets stay inaccessible to its agents; the test MAE is computed only in the external evaluation of the best method (paper Section 3.3 and Appendix B). A search that selects candidates by this score therefore selects on the test split; the validation MAE of each evaluation is reported as best_val_mae.

Measured (Apple M4 Max shared with other jobs, four threads): the seed (the Station's shared-neuron MLP baseline, 2,656 parameters, batch 8) scores 0.02908 after 3 epochs (validation MAE by epoch 0.03371, 0.03125, 0.03061); three evaluations took 305-434 s wall (training child 1048-1247 CPU-seconds, 96-143 s per epoch at load averages 8-20, peak memory 3.4 GB; scoring child about 15 s); a 5-epoch run reached 0.02889. For scale on the same test split: mean of context 0.03186, last value 0.03470, per-neuron training mean 0.03371; published ZAPBench values with this metric at context 4 (3 seeds): linear 0.02924, TSMixer 0.02814, UNet 0.02676; the Station reports 0.02662 for LLM-TS and 0.02637 for its own method. Scores here are not comparable with these values: models train for at most 3 CPU epochs, so larger models are under-trained and fast learners are favoured.

Determinism: three evaluations of the seed gave identical validation curves and test MAEs. A candidate whose epochs take longer than about 190 s may stop at the 600 s cap; its number of epochs then depends on machine speed (reported as stopped_by = time_cap). Memory: the training child may use up to 6 GB (the seed peaks at 3.4 GB), above the suite's 4 GB guideline, because 71,721-neuron windows and the baseline's per-neuron activations need it. valid is null: the score is the held-out error of a trained model, not a certified quantity.
